items.title: Catching Bugs Before They Land: JiTTesting’s Human-on-the-Loop Approach at Full Scale
items.abstract: Over the last year we’ve been sharing our work leveraging large language models to catch bugs on the fly — a novel approach we call Catching Just-in-Time Tests (JiTTests). Now, we’re sharing the results and positive impact we’ve seen with Catching JiTTests deployed into production. Our paper, “ Just-in-Time Catching Test Generation at Meta ,” fully details our initial deployment and testing with Catching JiTTests. Every code change improves our platform, but it also introduces new complexity. With hundreds of millions of lines of code constantly evolving at Meta, traditional testing can’t keep pace. Catching risks proactively, before code lands, enables us to identify risks earlier, respond more effectively, and deliver reliable experiences at scale. Over the last year, we’ve shared our research into applying large language models (LLMs) to generate software tests . More specifically, we’ve shared our work with Just-in-Time Tests (JiTTests) , a novel testing approach where we leverage LLMs to catch bugs on the fly, even ones that traditional testing might not catch. In the five months since we first unveiled this work, we’ve deployed our Catching JiTTests approach to determine its scalability and applicability to the wider industry. Today, Catching JiTTests are no longer a research prototype; they’re part of Meta’s infrastructure, and they’re helping our engineers catch more bugs with less load and a smaller chance of false positives. The Advantage of Catching JiTTests Most AI-based approaches to preventing bugs in code use LLMs and/or agentic AI to review code and detect faults based on prior experience. They work through the same review process that a human reviewer would, only faster. Catching JiTTests is a fundamentally different approach (Table 1): It generates executable tests that demonstrate a concrete behavioral difference introduced by the change. While it requires more computational steps, it catches classes of bugs that LLM- or agent-based code reviews might not. Table 1. Key differences between traditional LLM-based code review and Catching JiTTests. How We Implemented Catching JiTTests at Meta JiTTests are automatically generated and designed to fail, surfacing bugs in code changes (diffs) before they land in production. When they’re applied to a codebase as large as Meta’s, one challenge is distinguishing strong catches (i.e., true-positive failures that reveal real bugs) from weak catches (i.e., tests that may be false positives). It boils down to a specific question: For every proposed diff, how can we automatically generate tests that find the most severe bugs before they cause severe issues, and do so with a high true-positive rate and without impeding the velocity of our engineers? To address this, we developed two tandem workflows: An “intent-aware” workflow that infers the intention and risks of a code change and targets test generation toward likely failure points. A “dodgy diff” workflow that treats every code change as if it were a mutant/bug and generates tests to expose its behavioral differences without reasoning about intent. It implicitly asserts that a diff is buggy (hence the term “dodgy”). Figure 1. The architecture of the dodgy diff and intent-aware workflows for Catching JiTTests. To filter false positives, we employed a traditional rule-based approach combined with an ensemble approach we call “LLM-as-Judge,” which aggregates judgements from several state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs, all tasked with classifying weak catches as likely true or false positives. We also maintained human review, with an eye toward reducing review load. Our goal is to maintain the consistency of human labeling but reduce the likelihood of an engineer being brought in to review a weak catch. items.title_ko: Meta, LLM 기반 테스트 생성 JiTTests 전면 배포 — 코드 반영 전 버그 사전 포착, 리뷰 부담 감소
items.summary: Meta는 LLM으로 즉시 테스트를 생성해 코드 변경 시 버그를 사전에 잡는 'Catching JiTTests' 기법을 5개월간 실제 프로덕션에 배포해 검증했다. 이 방식은 코드 리뷰처럼 과거 경험 기반으로 결함을 추정하는 기존 LLM/에이전트 리뷰와 달리, 변경으로 인한 구체적 행동 차이를 입증하는 실행 가능한 테스트를 생성한다. 구현을 위해 변경 의도와 위험을 추론해 테스트를 생성하는 'intent-aware' 워크플로우와, 모든 diff를 버그로 간주하고 테스트를 생성하는 'dodgy diff' 워크플로우를 병행했다. 허위 양성을 걸러내기 위해 규칙 기반 필터와 여러 SOTA LLM의 판단을 종합하는 '**LLM-as-Judge**' 앙상블을 결합했고, 인간 검토는 유지하되 검토 부담을 줄이는 데 집중했다.
items.why_it_matters: 수억 줄 규모의 코드베이스에서 전통적 테스트로는 변화 속도를 따라가기 힘든 상황에서, 사전 예방적 버그 탐지가 엔지니어링 신뢰성과 속도를 동시에 지키는 실질적 해법이 될 수 있음을 보여준다.
items.whats_different: 기존 LLM/에이전트 기반 코드 리뷰가 사람처럼 경험적으로 결함을 추정하는 것과 달리, JiTTests는 **실행 가능한 테스트**로 행동 차이를 직접 증명해 리뷰 방식으로는 못 잡는 버그 유형을 포착한다.

items.title: How MoEngage turned over 400 APIs into agent tools with AgentCore Gateway
items.abstract: This post was co-written with Nikhil Kumar and Shakir Khan from MoEngage. When engineering teams start building AI agents, the capabilities those agents need usually already exist as internal APIs. Campaign creation, segment queries, delivery stats. The challenge isn’t building new functionality. The challenge is making hundreds of private APIs safely reachable by agents without exposing them to the public internet, without giving models control over identity, and without flooding context windows with hundreds of tool definitions. MoEngage, the agentic customer engagement platform that more than 1,350 consumer brands use to deliver personalized experiences across push, email, in-app, SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS, faced exactly this problem. Behind the product sit roughly 400 internal REST APIs, built by 25 engineering teams, running in private virtual private clouds (VPCs) across seven AWS Regions. MoEngage isolates these APIs regionally to meet data residency commitments and doesn’t expose them to the public internet. The capability the agents needed was already running in production. Making it reachable, safely, was the hard part. In this post, we walk through how MoEngage used AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to turn those private APIs into permission-scoped agent tools. The approach saved MoEngage an estimated six months of platform engineering effort, and onboarding a new API now takes hours instead of days. No product team wrote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server code, no networking was provisioned per integration, and no public endpoint exists anywhere in the path. Why 20 MCP servers was the wrong answer The Model Context Protocol (MCP) gives agents a standard way to discover and call tools. The straightforward path to adopting it is for each team to expose its own MCP server. MoEngage costed that out and rejected it. Over 20 MCP servers means over 20 deployments to monitor, patch, and keep protocol-compatible as MCP evolves. Cross-domain agents, the useful ones that read a campaign, check its segment, and inspect delivery stats, would need to connect to several servers and reconcile them. And every team would need MCP expertise unrelated to its actual product work. So MoEngage established the principle that shaped everything that followed: Individual engineering teams do not implement MCP. Teams build REST APIs and declare which operations should be tools. The AI Platform team owns the MCP layer end to end. A team’s responsibility ends at a well-described OpenAPI spec. That principle immediately created three requirements: a central tool surface that agents connect to once rather than per-service, per-agent authorization enforced server-side rather than by convention, and private connectivity that does not need to be rebuilt for every new API. Building all of this from scratch was an option. A custom central MCP server would solve the 20-servers problem but leave MoEngage building a tool-generation pipeline, a policy file format, a tool-alias registry for renames, and circuit breakers. All custom code, all owned by one team, all of it undifferentiated work that does not make MoEngage’s agents smarter or its customers’ campaigns better. Four constraints that shaped the architecture Before evaluating any solution, MoEngage defined four constraints. All four had to be met simultaneously. A solution that addressed two but broke the third and fourth was not viable. Nothing gets a public endpoint. MoEngage’s internal APIs are VPC-private by policy. Any solution that required exposing them, even behind additional authentication, was a non-starter. The conventional workaround is per-integration networking: a NAT gateway here, a reverse proxy there, a VPN tunnel for the third one. Multiply that by seven Regions and the operational surface grows faster than the set of agents does. items.summary: MoEngage는 25개 엔지니어링팀이 7개 AWS 리전의 프라이빗 VPC에서 운영하는 약 400개 내부 REST API를 AI 에이전트가 안전하게 사용할 수 있도록 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore의 AgentCore Gateway를 도입했다. 팀별로 20여 개의 MCP 서버를 각각 구축하는 방식은 배포·패치 부담과 MCP 전문성 요구로 인해 기각됐고, 대신 각 팀은 OpenAPI 스펙만 잘 작성하고 AI Platform팀이 MCP 레이어 전체를 중앙에서 소유하는 원칙을 세웠다. 이를 통해 공용 엔드포인트 없이, 서버 측 권한 제어와 프라이빗 연결을 유지하면서 에이전트 도구를 만들어냈다. 이 접근으로 **약 6개월의 플랫폼 엔지니어링 공수**를 절감했고, 새 API 온보딩이 수일에서 수시간으로 단축됐다.
items.why_it_matters: 내부 API가 이미 존재하는 조직이 에이전트를 도입할 때 겪는 핵심 난제, 즉 수백 개 API를 보안·규모 문제 없이 노출하는 방법을 실제 운영 사례로 보여준다. 팀별 MCP 서버 구축의 확장성 한계를 명확히 지적해 **중앙집중형 게이트웨이 설계**의 당위성을 제시한다.
items.whats_different: 팀마다 자체 MCP 서버를 만드는 기존의 분산형 접근 대비, 팀은 OpenAPI 스펙 작성까지만 책임지고 MCP 변환·권한·연결 계층은 AI Platform팀이 AgentCore Gateway로 중앙 관리하는 구조로 차별화된다.

items.title: Building intent-driven UI testing with Amazon Nova Act
items.abstract: To scale intent-driven UI testing across its product teams, Epsilon , a data, technology, and marketing-services company and part of Publicis Groupe , turned to Amazon Nova Act . With hundreds of millions of consumer profiles and thousands of brand relationships, Epsilon needed UI testing that could keep pace with rapid application changes. The solution could not create maintenance overhead for every product team. Within Epsilon, the Agentic Platform team (50 engineers) builds shared infrastructure so other product teams can build, deploy, govern, and run AI agents safely. With this shared platform, teams get a skills-based agent builder. They also get federated identity and pre-flight authorization, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration, and cross-account provisioning. When a product team wants to adopt AI tooling, they get capabilities without additional configuration and without re-solving identity, security, browser infrastructure, or model integration on their own. One of those managed capabilities is UI testing . With Amazon Nova Act and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser (a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore), Epsilon’s platform team could deliver resilient, intent-driven testing as a service to teams on the platform. In this post, we walk through Epsilon’s architecture for delivering UI testing as a managed platform service, show the core Nova Act and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool integration code, highlight a concrete 18-step test workflow, and share best practices and measured results. The challenge: Enhancing coverage, not replacing what works Epsilon’s existing UI testing practice was not broken. The team maintained a Playwright-based regression suite that validated functionality across their web applications, and it worked well. Playwright remains their regression backbone today. The opportunity Epsilon identified was additive, not corrective: Scripted Playwright tests are effective for deterministic regression checks. However, they are tightly coupled to selectors and page structure. Cosmetic UI changes can break them even when the underlying functionality is sound. Multiple product teams needed full testing coverage against their own applications. Standing up browser infrastructure, managing dependencies, and integrating with identity systems per team created duplicative effort. The platform team wanted UI testing to be a managed capability that fit their existing agent model, not a custom CLI that every onboarded team had to operate. The goal: layer intent-based testing on top of the existing Playwright regression suite. Deliver it as a multi-tenant platform service so that each Epsilon product team could consume through the same API surface they used for every other agent capability. Why Epsilon chose Amazon Nova Act and the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool Epsilon evaluated options against two requirements: natural-language test authoring (to complement selector-based Playwright tests) and managed browser infrastructure (to fit their multi-tenant platform model). With Amazon Nova Act combined with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool, Epsilon could address both. Natural-language steps. Test steps are plain-English instructions executed by Nova Act. They are resilient to cosmetic UI changes and readable by non-engineers. A step like “Confirm the rewards balance is visible” ages far better than a brittle CSS selector. AWS managed, ephemeral browser sessions. With Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool, teams get isolated browser instances with no binaries to ship and no display server to maintain. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool also offers live view for human observation or takeover (useful for CAPTCHAs or multi-factor authentication), session recording to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), and AWS CloudTrail audit, all without additional configuration. items.summary: Epsilon은 수억 명의 소비자 프로필과 수천 개 브랜드 관계를 다루는 환경에서, 제품팀마다 UI 테스트 인프라를 중복 구축하지 않도록 사내 **Agentic Platform 팀**이 공유 에이전트 인프라를 구축했다. 기존 Playwright 기반 회귀 테스트는 그대로 유지하되, 선택자에 의존해 사소한 UI 변경에도 깨지는 한계를 보완하기 위해 Amazon Nova Act와 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool을 결합한 의도 기반 테스트를 추가했다. Nova Act는 "리워드 잔액이 보이는지 확인"과 같은 자연어 지시문으로 테스트를 실행해 UI 변경에 강건하고 비개발자도 이해할 수 있다. AgentCore Browser Tool은 격리된 일회성 브라우저 세션, 라이브 뷰, S3 세션 기록, CloudTrail 감사 기능을 제공해 별도 설정 없이 멀티테넌트 플랫폼 서비스로 제공 가능하다. 이 글은 18단계 테스트 워크플로와 핵심 통합 코드, 운영 모범사례 및 측정 결과를 소개한다.
items.why_it_matters: 선택자 기반 테스트의 유지보수 부담을 자연어 지시문으로 낮추면서도 기존 회귀 테스트 체계를 대체하지 않고 보완하는 현실적인 도입 사례로, 여러 제품팀이 동일한 API로 AI 에이전트 기능을 소비하는 **플랫폼화 전략**을 보여준다.
items.whats_different: 기존 Playwright 기반 선택자 테스트는 페이지 구조에 강하게 결합돼 사소한 UI 변경에도 깨지는 반면, Nova Act는 자연어 단계로 테스트를 기술해 코스메틱 변경에 강건하고 팀별 브라우저 인프라·신원 통합을 별도로 구축할 필요가 없다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Detecting Brain Cancer Progression Through Signatures of Wearable Accelerometry Data
items.abstract: Glioblastoma and other high-grade gliomas (HGG) have a poor prognosis and are associated with progressive functional decline. The standard of care to assess progressive disease is contrast-enhanced MRI, which is expensive, claustrophobic, and performed only once every 2-3 months. Wearable accelerometers offer a non-invasive alternative for continuously monitoring patient function between clinic visits. However, accelerometry data streams are typically noisy and highly patient-specific, making conventional time series methods and summary statistics poorly suited to detecting clinically meaningful change. This work aims to classify stable versus progressive disease states by applying rough path signatures for feature extraction from wrist-worn accelerometer data. We convert accelerometer recordings from HGG patients enrolled in the BrainWear study into walking-path segments and use signature kernel maximum mean discrepancy (SigMMD) to quantify change in patients' walking behaviour. We overcome the challenge of inter-patient heterogeneity by adjusting for the natural variation in a patient's walking during stable tumour periods. This patient-specific normalisation substantially improves separation, yielding a candidate biomarker of tumour progression. Our results provide proof-of-concept evidence that signature-based analysis of wearable accelerometry can distinguish stable from progressive disease states, motivating larger longitudinal studies of continuous wearable monitoring as a digital biomarker in neuro-oncology.
items.title_ko: 손목 가속도계 신호에 rough path signature 적용, 뇌종양(HGG) 안정기 대 진행기 구분 가능성 제시
items.summary: 고등급 신경교종(HGG) 환자는 기능이 점진적으로 악화되지만, 표준 진단법인 조영증강 MRI는 비싸고 2~3개월에 한 번만 시행된다는 한계가 있다. 이 연구는 손목 착용형 가속도계 데이터를 걷기 구간으로 변환하고 rough path signature 기반 SigMMD(signature kernel maximum mean discrepancy)로 보행 패턴 변화를 정량화했다. 환자마다 걷기 양상이 크게 다른 문제는 **안정기 동안의 개인별 보행 변동으로 정규화**해 해결했으며, 이 환자별 정규화가 안정기와 진행기 구분을 크게 개선했다. BrainWear 연구 참여 환자 데이터를 통해 이 신호 기반 분석이 종양 진행의 후보 바이오마커가 될 수 있음을 proof-of-concept 수준에서 보였다.
items.why_it_matters: MRI처럼 비용이 크고 간헐적인 검사 대신 웨어러블로 연속 모니터링이 가능해지면 신경종양학에서 디지털 바이오마커 개발의 새로운 방향이 열릴 수 있다. 노이즈가 많고 환자별 편차가 큰 의료 시계열 데이터를 다루는 데 signature 방법론이 유효하다는 근거를 제공한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 요약통계 기반 시계열 분석 대비, 노이즈가 많고 환자마다 상이한 가속도계 데이터에 rough path signature와 SigMMD를 적용하고 **환자별 안정기 변동으로 정규화**하는 접근이 다르다.

items.title: Speeding up language models for travel applications
items.abstract: Travel platforms serve millions of daily users by answering questions about destinations, offering hotel recommendations, and helping users plan their trips. In recent years, many platforms have turned to large language models (LLMs) to improve these services. The LLMs give accurate, contextually relevant travel advice thanks to their size: they typically have tens of billions of parameters. Unfortunately, such large models are also computationally expensive, and that expense scales with the number of customer queries. What’s more, such large models can be too slow for web and mobile applications, where a delay of even 100 milliseconds can cost a company customers and revenue. To address these scaling and latency challenges, we explored two complementary optimization techniques. One is a compression technique known as knowledge distillation (KD), in which a slow but powerful model produces training targets for a faster, lightweight model. The other, called Medusa, is a framework that transforms sequential next-token predictions — a common bottleneck in LLMs — into parallel computations. Working with leading online travel agency Booking.com, we applied KD and Medusa techniques to the LLMs that power various aspects of its user experience, looking to improve either latency or cost effectiveness. We focused on three features in particular: The AI Trip Planner: A conversational assistant that must extract travel preferences from dialogue in less than a second (latency); Smart Filters: A feature that converts natural-language search queries into structured information filters in real time (latency); Accommodation Description Generation: A feature that produces property descriptions on the scale of millions of listings (cost effectiveness). We demonstrated that combining both KD and Medusa maintains the quality of the best open-source LLMs at less than one-third the cost while running up to 20 times as fast. Our framework ensures that travel platforms or other applications that rely on LLMs can deliver fast, cost-effective, accurate responses in real-world scenarios. We presented these techniques at last year’s meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), where it received the Industry Track best-paper award. Our approach: Medusa plus knowledge distillation Medusa is a framework designed to reduce LLM latency in real-time applications such as chat and code generation. It improves computational efficiency at run time — inference time — rather than during training. Ordinarily, an LLM generates text one token — word or word part — at a time. Medusa accelerates this process by predicting multiple tokens in parallel. Medusa does this by adding prediction modules, called Medusa heads, to the base LLM, one head for each token decoded in parallel. GPU hardware that LLMs run on is optimized for parallelism, so it can handle parallel token decoding with little additional overhead. Medusa offers significant speedups, typically 2-4-fold without compromising generation quality. Knowledge distillation addresses the deployment challenges of large, parameter-heavy models by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models to smaller “student” models. Typically, a teacher model is first trained or fine-tuned on high-quality labeled data, then used to generate predictions on additional unlabeled data. The manually labeled and machine-labeled data are then combined to train a smaller student model, which learns to mimic the teacher’s behavior. The student model retains much of the teacher’s performance but is significantly more efficient, making it better suited for real-world scenarios such as high-volume consumer-facing websites. In our work, we integrate KD and Medusa in a unified pipeline starting with pretrained base models. As in standard KD, we fine-tune the teacher on the labeled dataset and use it to generate predictions on unlabeled, domain-relevant text. items.title_ko: Amazon·Booking.com, 지식증류+Medusa 결합해 여행 LLM 속도 20배·비용 3분의1로 단축
items.summary: Amazon이 Booking.com과 협력해 여행 플랫폼용 LLM의 지연시간과 비용 문제를 해결하는 최적화 기법을 소개했다. 느리지만 성능 좋은 teacher 모델의 예측을 작은 student 모델에 학습시키는 지식증류(KD)와, 토큰을 순차가 아닌 병렬로 예측하게 하는 Medusa 프레임워크를 결합했다. AI Trip Planner, Smart Filters, 숙소 설명 생성 등 세 가지 기능에 적용한 결과, 두 기법을 함께 쓰면 오픈소스 LLM 수준의 품질을 유지하면서 **비용은 3분의 1 이하, 속도는 최대 20배**까지 개선했다. 이 연구는 ACL 산업 트랙 최우수 논문상을 수상했다.
items.why_it_matters: 수백만 사용자가 실시간으로 응답을 받아야 하는 소비자 대상 서비스에서 100밀리초의 지연도 매출에 영향을 줄 수 있어, 대형 LLM을 실서비스에 배치할 때 발생하는 비용·속도 문제를 실제 업계 사례로 보여준다.
items.whats_different: KD와 Medusa를 각각 별도로 적용하는 기존 방식과 달리, teacher 모델 미세조정 후 student 모델 학습 단계에 Medusa 헤드를 함께 붙이는 **통합 파이프라인**으로 두 기법의 이점을 동시에 얻는다.

items.title: Unlocking Tensor Core Performance for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
items.abstract: Atomistic simulations help researchers understand how molecules and materials behave, from chemical reactions and phase transitions to mechanical failure. These... Atomistic simulations help researchers understand how molecules and materials behave, from chemical reactions and phase transitions to mechanical failure. These simulations come with a cost-accuracy trade-off. Quantum-mechanical methods such as density functional theory (DFT) can provide accurate energies and forces, but their computational cost often limits their use for large systems or long… Source
items.title_ko: NVIDIA, 머신러닝 원자간 포텐셜에 Tensor Core 가속 적용 — DFT 수준 정확도·속도 격차 해소 시도
items.summary: 이 글은 분자·재료의 거동을 연구하는 원자 단위 시뮬레이션에서 비용-정확도 트레이드오프 문제를 다룬다. 밀도범함수이론(DFT) 같은 양자역학 기반 방법은 정확한 에너지·힘을 제공하지만 계산 비용이 커서 대규모 시스템이나 장시간 시뮬레이션에는 한계가 있다고 설명한다. 이를 보완하기 위해 머신러닝 기반 원자간 포텐셜(MLIP)을 활용하는 접근을 소개하며, NVIDIA의 **Tensor Core**를 활용해 성능을 끌어올리는 방법을 다룬다.
items.why_it_matters: DFT 수준의 정확도를 유지하면서 대규모·장시간 시뮬레이션이 가능해지면 재료 설계와 화학 반응 연구의 실험 주기를 크게 단축할 수 있다.

items.title: Floor It, Then Fill It: Simulating Creator Ecosystems for Fair Video-Content Recommendation Systems at Billion User Scale
items.abstract: Engagement-optimized content recommendation systems exhibit a well-documented rich-get-richer dynamic that structurally disadvantages emerging creators on large-scale platforms. Evaluating debiasing interventions at scale demands faithful simulation of creator-viewer ecosystems, yet the fidelity, diversity, and validity of such simulators remain underexplored. We present a grounded user-simulation framework that models a heterogeneous population of ${\sim}42$K creators and their coupled viewer interactions over 12~weeks, and use it to evaluate equitable view-allocation policies formulated as a budgeted multi-armed bandit (MAB). The simulator captures three behavioral dimensions: (i)~\textbf{creator diversity}, modeled via a clustering approach grounded in real platform creator-level distributions; (ii)~\textbf{behavioral fidelity}, captured through coupled creator-content state machines that represent growth trajectories, engagement accumulation, and graduation dynamics; and (iii)~\textbf{population-level validity}, measured by calibration against observed platform metrics. We evaluate simulative-configurations that vary content-viewership target definitions, reward functions, and a small-creator reserve lever to maximize creator-content recommendation equity. A floor-protected per content-view-target with a view-parity-gap reward guarantees 90\% of view targets being met by creators every week, grows small-creator organic reach ${\sim}{+}33\%$ per week, and achieves high distribution stability (set of creators with funded-views Jaccard $= 0.819$). We analyze the Sim2Real gap and propose validation protocols, contributing evidence for when simulation-derived fairness conclusions can be trusted.
items.title_ko: 대형 플랫폼 공정 추천 실험, 4.2만 창작자 시뮬레이션으로 소규모 창작자 노출 +33%/주 달성
items.summary: 이 논문은 참여도 최적화 추천 시스템이 신규·소규모 창작자를 구조적으로 불리하게 만드는 '부익부' 현상을 완화하기 위해, 약 4만2천 명 창작자와 시청자 상호작용을 12주간 모사하는 시뮬레이션 프레임워크를 제시한다. 시뮬레이터는 창작자 다양성(클러스터링), 행동 충실도(성장·참여 누적·졸업을 나타내는 상태 머신), 모집단 수준 타당성(실제 플랫폼 지표와의 보정)이라는 세 요소를 반영한다. 공정한 노출 배분 정책은 예산 제약형 멀티암드 밴딧(MAB)으로 정식화되어 평가되며, 콘텐츠별 조회수 목표 설정 방식, 보상 함수, 소규모 창작자 예약 레버 등 다양한 구성을 비교한다. 플로어 보호형 조회 목표와 조회 형평성 격차 보상을 결합한 정책은 **매주 창작자 90%의 조회 목표 달성**을 보장하고, 소규모 창작자의 자연 도달률을 주당 약 +33% 증가시키며, 분포 안정성(Jaccard 0.819)도 높게 유지했다. 저자들은 Sim2Real 격차를 분석하고 시뮬레이션 기반 공정성 결론을 신뢰할 수 있는 조건에 대한 검증 프로토콜을 제안한다.
items.why_it_matters: 수십억 사용자 규모 플랫폼에서는 디바이어싱 정책을 실제 서비스에 바로 적용하기 어려워 신뢰할 수 있는 시뮬레이션 환경 구축이 선행 과제인데, 이 연구는 그 신뢰성 검증 방법 자체를 다룬다는 점에서 실무적 의미가 크다. 추천 공정성 개입의 효과를 과대·과소평가하지 않기 위한 Sim2Real 검증 절차는 업계 전반에 적용 가능한 참고 사례가 될 수 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존 추천 공정성 연구가 정적 데이터셋이나 단순 가정에 기반한 시뮬레이션에 의존했던 것과 달리, 이 연구는 실제 플랫폼의 창작자 분포에 기반한 클러스터링과 창작자-콘텐츠 결합 상태 머신으로 **행동 충실도**를 확보하고, 플랫폼 지표와의 보정(calibration)을 통한 모집단 수준 타당성 검증을 함께 제시한다는 점에서 차별화된다.

items.title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract: Clinical large language models are increasingly fielded as multi-agent teams, on the assumption that deliberation averages out individual error. It does not average out bias. Across a full factorial of five model families and four aggregation topologies on 120 real MIMIC-IV emergency cases under counterfactual demographic swaps, no configuration neutralizes the disparity: all 20 cells commit the direction of their agents' independent answers, giving Black patients more acute triage. Every model has a topology that amplifies its baseline gap, but which one varies by model, so no design is reliably safe or reliably amplifying: the disparity is relocated, never removed. Late-stage fixes fail: fairness instructions and demographic masking leave the gap untouched, and per-agent self-debiasing widens it, because the bias is already encoded in the agents' ordinary clinical numbers. We call this disparity laundering; the audits now applied to clinical AI, per model, per output, per version, can certify the parts but never the committed decision. Interventions close the gap exactly when they make counterfactual versions visible inside the system and pool them, through deliberation, into the committed decision. A diverse-perspective ensemble does both while keeping the team, with no retraining or architectural change: the disparity falls by 67 to 94% where all five perspectives pool at every round, and the one topology that never pools them is the one it cannot reliably repair. Medical multi-agent systems do not filter demographic bias; they launder it into plausible decisions no single-version audit can catch, and the only defense is to make the bias visible.
items.title_ko: 임상 멀티에이전트 LLM, 합의해도 편향 안 사라져—20개 전 구성서 흑인 환자 과잉 트리아지, 다양 관점 앙상블로 67~94% 감소
items.summary: 5개 모델군과 4개 집계 토폴로지를 모두 조합해 실제 MIMIC-IV 응급 사례 120건에 반사실적 인구통계 교체를 적용했지만, **20개 구성 전부**에서 개별 에이전트의 편향 방향을 그대로 따라가 흑인 환자를 더 급성으로 분류했다. 각 모델마다 기존 편향을 증폭시키는 토폴로지가 있지만 모델별로 다르게 나타나, 편향은 제거되지 않고 자리만 옮겨 다닐 뿐이었다. 공정성 지시문, 인구통계 마스킹 같은 후처리 대응은 효과가 없었고, 에이전트별 자가 디바이어싱은 오히려 격차를 더 키웠는데, 이는 편향이 이미 각 에이전트의 일반 임상 판단 수치에 내재되어 있기 때문이다. 반면 반사실적 버전들을 시스템 내부에서 보이게 하고 숙의를 통해 통합하는 개입, 즉 다양한 관점을 모든 라운드에서 풀링하는 앙상블 방식은 재훈련이나 구조 변경 없이 격차를 **67~94% 감소**시켰다.
items.why_it_matters: 임상 AI에 적용되는 모델별·출력별 감사는 개별 요소는 검증할 수 있어도 최종 합의 결정에 숨은 편향은 잡아내지 못한다는 점에서, 멀티에이전트 설계가 편향을 걸러내는 게 아니라 '세탁'해 버릴 위험을 보여준다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 공정성 지시문이나 인구통계 마스킹, 개별 에이전트 자가 디바이어싱 같은 사후 교정 방식과 달리, 반사실적 관점을 시스템 내부에서 명시적으로 드러내고 숙의 과정에서 풀링하는 접근만이 격차를 실질적으로 줄였다.

items.title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program
items.abstract: Solving large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs (mpQPs) in real time often requires thousands of iterative optimization updates, creating a major computational bottleneck in model predictive control and learning-enabled systems. This paper proposes TQPNet, a self-supervised neural compression framework that learns to compress long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. We derive a low-dimensional ADMM scheme operating on the primal-dual variables $(x,β)$ and show that its iteration admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, termed ADMM(ReLU). Building on this insight, TQPNet combines a multilayer perceptron with ReLU activations (MLP(ReLU)) and a small number of unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers. The network is trained offline using an optimality-condition-informed residual loss, eliminating the need for solver-generated labels. The proposed residual-based framework enables both self-supervised training and online solution certification through adaptive ADMM(ReLU) refinement. Experiments on large-scale mpQPs and real-time MPC applications demonstrate that TQPNet achieves high accuracy, strong generalization, and substantially faster inference than conventional optimization-based methods.
items.title_ko: TQPNet, ADMM 긴 최적화 궤적을 신경망으로 압축 — mpQP 실시간 풀이 가속
items.summary: 이 논문은 대규모 다변수 2차계획법(mpQP)을 실시간으로 풀기 위해 수천 번의 ADMM 반복이 필요한 문제를 해결하고자 TQPNet을 제안한다. 저primal-dual 변수 (x,β) 상에서 동작하는 저차원 ADMM 기법을 유도하고, 그 반복 과정이 ReLU 레이어로 등가 표현됨(ADMM(ReLU))을 보인다. TQPNet은 ReLU 활성화 MLP와 소수의 unrolled ADMM(ReLU) 정제 레이어를 결합해 긴 최적화 궤적을 압축된 신경망 웜스타트로 변환한다. 솔버가 생성한 레이블 없이 **최적성 조건 기반 잔차 손실**로 오프라인 학습하며, 이 잔차 기반 프레임워크는 자기지도 학습과 온라인 해 검증(적응형 ADMM(ReLU) 정제)을 동시에 가능하게 한다. 대규모 mpQP 및 실시간 MPC 실험에서 기존 최적화 기반 방법보다 높은 정확도와 일반화, **훨씬 빠른 추론 속도**를 달성했다.
items.why_it_matters: 모델예측제어(MPC)나 학습 기반 시스템에서 실시간 최적화는 주요 병목인데, 이를 신경망 웜스타트로 대체하면 제어 주기 내 연산 부담을 크게 줄일 수 있어 실용적 가치가 크다.
items.whats_different: 기존 ADMM 반복 기반 최적화 솔버 대비, ADMM 반복 자체를 ReLU 레이어로 재해석해 신경망에 내재화하고 솔버 레이블 없이 잔차 손실만으로 자기지도 학습한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Interpretable and Validatable Uplift Modeling
items.abstract: Uplift models estimate treatment effects for individuals, but we do not observe individual treatment effects, so the predictions are hard to interpret and validate. A decision-maker often wants trustworthy claims about groups where the treatment is beneficial or harmful, and to know when a treatment benefits some people more than others. Our procedure provides such a set of claims, certified simultaneously at a specified familywise error rate (FWER). We summarize an uplift model by a shallow tree fit to its predictions. Each node of the tree carries two hypotheses, one about the average treatment effect in the node and one about the difference in effects across the node's split; the two kinds are interwoven into a single hierarchy. Splitting the data enables honest estimation in the evaluation set. It lets us choose the direction of each one-sided test from the training half, allowing us to certify the sign of treatment effects in subpopulations, and to compare effects between groups. We demonstrate our procedure offers strong control of the FWER.
items.title_ko: 업리프트 모델, 얕은 트리와 가족별 오류율(FWER) 제어로 해석·검증 가능하게 만들다
items.summary: 업리프트 모델은 개인별 처치 효과를 예측하지만 실제 개인 효과는 관측 불가능해 결과 해석과 검증이 어렵다. 이 연구는 업리프트 모델의 예측값을 얕은 트리로 요약하고, 각 노드에 평균 처치 효과에 대한 가설과 분기 간 효과 차이에 대한 가설을 함께 부여하는 방법을 제안한다. 데이터를 학습용과 평가용으로 분할함으로써 검정 방향을 학습 세트에서 정하고 평가 세트에서는 정직한 추정을 수행해, 하위집단에서의 처치 효과 부호를 증명하고 집단 간 효과를 비교할 수 있다. 제안된 절차는 **가족별 오류율(FWER)**을 지정된 수준에서 동시에 강하게 제어함을 실험으로 보인다.
items.why_it_matters: 업리프트 모델의 예측은 그 자체로 검증 불가능한 경우가 많아, 어떤 하위집단에서 처치가 실제로 이롭거나 해로운지 신뢰할 수 있게 주장하는 방법이 실무 의사결정에 중요하다.
items.whats_different: 기존 업리프트 모델이 개별 예측값만 제시하는 것과 달리, 이 방법은 트리 구조와 데이터 분할 기반의 정직한 추정을 통해 하위집단별 효과 부호와 집단 간 차이를 **FWER 통제 하에** 동시에 검증 가능한 형태로 제시한다.

items.title: Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs
items.abstract: With the launch of AWS Batch support for Amazon SageMaker Training jobs, customers gained a new fully managed way to queue, schedule, and retry machine learning (ML) training workloads without building their own infrastructure. Instead, they use the queuing and scheduling features of AWS Batch. As organizations scale their artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) operations and onboard more teams, coordinating access to shared graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity can introduce additional communication, coordination, and configuration overhead for administrators. This overhead includes setting up separate queues, adjusting capacity limits, and carefully orchestrating the right workloads to get the right resources at the right time. A core value proposition of AWS Batch is helping customers increase utilization of their compute, and as training environments grow, so does the opportunity to do more with existing capacity. Working backward from customers managing multi-team training environments, we heard a consistent request: give us a way to define allocations per team or project, share idle capacity automatically, and run our highest-priority workloads first. This request led us to build quota management , a new scheduling capability for AWS Batch. Administrators can use it to divide compute capacity into quota shares, organized by team, project, or workload. Each quota share uses configurable resource-sharing strategies that maximize GPU utilization while honoring each team’s allocation when it matters most. This post shows how quota management works, including how to configure quota shares with lending and borrowing strategies, set up in-share preemption for priority workloads, and get started using the SageMaker Python SDK. Quota shares and preemption Administrators can allocate and share constrained GPU resources by defining a quota share for separate entities, such as individual teams or projects. Each quota share includes compute quotas (capacity limits) and resource-sharing strategies for idle compute. These strategies determine whether idle compute is reserved until jobs arrive ( RESERVE ), lent to other quota shares that have work available ( LEND ), or both lent when idle and borrowed when the share has work that might benefit ( LEND_AND_BORROW ). A quota share operates as a virtual queue nested hierarchically within an associated job queue. When scheduling jobs for a job queue, AWS Batch prioritizes quota shares that are under their capacity limits as it iterates through the associated quota shares. If jobs arrive in a quota share that has lent out its capacity, AWS Batch performs cross-share preemption. This reclaims resources for the lending quota share, so administrators don’t need to track down the jobs borrowing capacity and terminate them on their own. If jobs arrive in a quota share that is at or above its capacity limit, AWS Batch checks whether there’s available capacity to borrow from another quota share. If so, workloads can run using otherwise-idle capacity. You can turn on priority-based in-share preemption when you configure a quota share. Where cross-share preemption reclaims lent capacity as jobs arrive in a lending quota share, in-share preemption preempts lower priority jobs that are in the SCHEDULED, STARTING, or RUNNING state. This allows higher priority jobs at the front of the queue to start running sooner. Prerequisites Before you proceed with this example, you must have an AWS account with permissions to create and manage AWS Batch resources. For this example, see the sample IAM permissions needed to invoke AWS Batch and SageMaker APIs. The example uses the SageMaker Python SDK v3. items.title_ko: AWS Batch, SageMaker Training에 쿼터 관리 기능 추가 — 팀 간 GPU 자원 대여·차용 자동화
items.summary: AWS Batch가 SageMaker Training 작업을 위한 쿼터 관리 기능을 새로 지원한다. 관리자는 팀·프로젝트별로 컴퓨트 용량을 쿼터 셰어로 나누고, **RESERVE, LEND, LEND_AND_BORROW** 같은 자원 공유 전략을 설정해 유휴 GPU를 자동으로 빌려주거나 빌려올 수 있다. 쿼터 셰어가 유휴 용량을 빌려준 상태에서 새 작업이 도착하면 AWS Batch가 크로스 셰어 선점을 수행해 자동으로 자원을 회수하며, 셰어 내 우선순위 기반 선점도 설정해 높은 우선순위 작업을 먼저 실행할 수 있다. SageMaker Python SDK를 통해 스케줄링 정책과 서비스 환경을 구성하는 방식으로 사용을 시작한다.
items.why_it_matters: 여러 팀이 GPU 자원을 공유하는 조직에서는 큐 설정과 용량 조정, 워크로드 우선순위 조율에 관리 오버헤드가 크게 발생하는데, 이 기능은 이를 자동화해 **GPU 활용률**을 높이는 데 도움을 준다.
items.whats_different: 기존에는 관리자가 별도 큐를 수동으로 구성하고 자원을 빌려간 작업을 직접 추적해 종료해야 했지만, 이번 쿼터 관리는 **자동 크로스 셰어 선점**을 통해 관리자의 수동 개입 없이 자원을 회수한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Integral Probability Boundaries
items.abstract: Bounds based on Integral Probability Metrics (IPMs) are ubiquitous in machine learning and statistics, appearing, e.g., in generalization, alignment, fairness, and privacy. IPMs reduce the discrepancy between two distributions to a single worst-case gap between expectations. This compression is costly: for rare events, safety failures, or under-represented groups, IPM-based bounds are loose or vacuous. We introduce a non-linear generalization of IPMs, which we term Integral Probability Boundaries (IPBs). Unlike IPMs, IPBs provide bounds that are tight at the extremes. We derive their basic properties and present algorithms for estimating them in practically relevant settings. We demonstrate the usage of IPBs in both theoretical and practical applications for alignment, judge-free performance estimation, and fairness, where they enable us to obtain sharp bounds on performance and fairness gaps, e.g., 15 p.p. more precise estimates on fairness gaps for rare groups in a realistic generative modeling task, compared to the state of the art.
items.title_ko: NeurIPS 2026, IPM 일반화한 'Integral Probability Boundaries' 제안 — 희귀 그룹 공정성 격차 추정 15%p 개선
items.summary: 기존 Integral Probability Metrics(IPM)는 두 분포 간 차이를 하나의 최악 기댓값 격차로 압축하는데, 이는 희귀 이벤트나 소수 그룹에서는 느슨하거나 공허한 경계를 낳는다. 이 논문은 IPM을 비선형으로 일반화한 Integral Probability Boundaries(IPB)를 제안하며, 극단값에서도 **타이트한 경계**를 제공한다. 저자들은 IPB의 기본 성질을 유도하고 실용적 환경에서 이를 추정하는 알고리즘을 제시한다. 정렬(alignment), 판정자 없는 성능 추정, 공정성 등에 IPB를 적용해 성능·공정성 격차에 대한 날카로운 경계를 얻을 수 있음을 보인다. 실제 생성 모델링 과제에서 희귀 그룹의 공정성 격차 추정이 기존 최선 대비 **15%p 더 정밀**함을 보였다.
items.why_it_matters: 일반화, 정렬, 공정성, 프라이버시 등 ML 전반에서 쓰이는 IPM 기반 경계가 소수 그룹·희귀 사건에서 무용지물이 될 수 있다는 점을 지적하고 이를 보완하므로, 공정성 감사나 안전성 평가의 신뢰도를 높이는 데 실질적 영향을 줄 수 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존 IPM이 분포 차이를 단일 최악 기댓값 격차로 압축해 희귀 사건·소수 그룹에서 경계가 느슨해지는 것과 달리, IPB는 비선형 일반화를 통해 극단값에서도 타이트한 경계를 제공한다.

items.title: The Indian Financial Automated Advice Bias (IFAAB) Dataset : Auditing Socioeconomic and Demographic Disparities in LLM-Generated Financial Advice in India
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for financial guidance, yet little is known about whether their advice changes across social identities in Global South contexts. We introduce the Indian Financial Automated Advice Bias (IFAAB) benchmark, a counterfactual audit dataset of 31,734 GPT-4o-generated financial-advice responses for synthetic Indian personas varying by gender, caste, education, employment, residence, age, and district. Holding the underlying request fixed, we evaluate disparities in LLM-implied wealth, income, savings, projected gains, textual similarity, advice topics, and qualitative bias judgments. In the gender-only audit, male-labelled profiles receive 60.1\% higher initial total resources and 46.8\% higher post-advice total resources than comparable female-labelled profiles; in the caste-augmented audit, the post-advice total-resource gap remains 49.4\%. Adding district information reduces the aggregate post-advice total-resource gender gap to 7.9\%, revealing strong geographic conditioning. Standalone caste comparisons also show systematic stratification: relative to General-category profiles, OBC, SC, and ST profiles receive significantly lower post-advice total resources, respectively. Textual audits show low semantic similarity between paired gendered responses, with an average TF--IDF cosine similarity score of 0.44. Qualitative analysis shows that women are more often steered toward cautious saving, community support, and basic financial literacy, while men receive more growth-oriented advice involving investment, entrepreneurship, and asset accumulation. IFAAB provides a reusable benchmark for evaluating fairness, suitability, and consumer-protection risks in LLM-mediated financial advice, and highlights the need for locally grounded, intersectional evaluation of AI systems in high-stakes economic domains.
items.title_ko: IFAAB 벤치마크 공개 — GPT-4o 금융 조언, 여성 페르소나에 남성 대비 자산 46.8% 적게 추천
items.summary: 연구진은 성별, 카스트, 학력, 직업, 거주지, 나이, 지역구별로 다른 인도인 가상 페르소나 31,734개에 대해 GPT-4o가 생성한 금융 조언을 비교하는 IFAAB 벤치마크를 구축했다. 동일한 질문에도 남성 페르소나는 여성 대비 조언 전 자산이 60.1%, 조언 후 자산이 46.8% 더 높게 산정됐고, 카스트를 추가한 분석에서도 조언 후 자산 격차가 49.4%로 유지됐다. 지역구 정보를 추가하면 성별 격차가 7.9%로 크게 줄어들어 **지리적 요인이 강한 교란변수**임이 드러났다. 카스트별로는 일반 카테고리 대비 OBC, SC, ST 페르소나 모두 조언 후 자산이 유의하게 낮았다. 또한 여성에게는 저축·공동체 지원·기초 금융지식 위주로, 남성에게는 투자·창업·자산축적 등 성장지향적 조언이 주어지는 질적 편향도 확인됐다.
items.why_it_matters: LLM 기반 금융 조언이 실제 소비자 상담에 쓰이기 시작하는 상황에서, **사회경제적 정체성에 따른 체계적 편향**이 소비자 보호와 공정성 문제로 직결된다는 점을 실증한 사례다. 인도처럼 카스트·젠더 격차가 뚜렷한 글로벌 사우스 맥락에서의 지역 특화 평가 필요성을 보여준다.
items.whats_different: 기존 LLM 공정성 평가가 주로 영어권·서구 맥락의 단일 속성(성별 또는 인종) 편향에 집중했던 것과 달리, IFAAB는 카스트·지역구·교육 등 인도 특유의 변수를 교차시켜 반사실적(counterfactual) 감사 데이터셋을 구축했다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro
items.abstract: When your team moves a mature PHP application to Java, you gain stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling. A PHP codebase built over the years with Laravel, Symfony, or Doctrine carries business rules in places that are not obvious, from Eloquent traits to XML mapping files, so a structurally similar Java port can compile cleanly and still behave differently. This post shows how to turn PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process using Kiro . Kiro is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) that pairs an AI agent with your codebase to run multi-step engineering tasks with you in the loop. The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight-phase workflow. This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it. Prerequisites Before getting started, you need: Familiarity with PHP (Laravel/Eloquent or Symfony/Doctrine). Java knowledge (Spring Boot, JPA) helps you review the generated output, but the engine produces idiomatic Java for you, so you don’t need to rewrite the application in Java yourself. A Kiro workspace with access to Skills and Steering files. PHP 8.0 or newer on the machine running the discovery scanner, and Java 21 with Maven for the generated Spring Boot projects. A basic understanding of migration planning (discovery, translation, and validation). What you will learn in this post You start with an open repository, so you can run the engine yourself rather than read about it. Everything the engine knows lives in a small set of skill files, and with those files, you can run the same methodology in more than one way. Two ways to run the engine: Kiro and AWS Transform Everything here is packaged as skill files: versioned Markdown capability packages that encode the migration methodology (php-to-java-migration) and the discovery scanner workflow (php-model-discovery). Because that knowledge lives in files rather than any one tool, you can run the same methodology in two ways. Method 1: Kiro, interactive and developer-in-the-loop Kiro brings an AI agent into your editor to drive a migration step by step. Open the repository root as a Kiro workspace and the skills activate automatically when you ask Kiro to migrate a PHP application. Kiro then walks the eight-phase workflow with explicit approval gates, so you review the discovery manifest, approve the rulebook, and sign off on each phase before the next begins. It’s the mode used for every example in this post. Method 2: AWS Transform, agentic and at portfolio scale AWS Transform is the AWS agentic AI service for large-scale migration and modernization, and it now integrates natively with Kiro. Through that integration, you can hand AWS Transform the same skill files that govern an interactive Kiro session, so discovery before translation, the parity harness as referee, and ‘ fix the loop, not the code ’ apply to an autonomous run. When each path fits Control and autonomy: Use Kiro to work through the code first: run the skill on one application, read the generated Java, and run the tests. When you want to migrate more, AWS Transform runs the same methodology agentically with review at the checkpoints the skill defines. Scale and novelty: Kiro handles one application at a time and suits first-of-a-kind frameworks. AWS Transform runs many applications as parallel jobs. A shared feedback loop: Both paths read the same skill files, so every rulebook fix made in Kiro improves the next AWS Transform run, and vice versa. Solution overview: One shared brain, many projects The engine is organized around a single principle: one shared brain, many projects.
